![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/3d51eade27c19494ac30ffdaf5baf8d30ffc9d18dcc3e1186cbc59412fe000c7.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,0\le y\le x+2}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=x+2\,⟹\,x=y-2,
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,y-2\le x\le 0},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/39072bd4c2d4bd763186f4d86921eaacb990df1e862f1c60b1f764ccff422e98.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{x+2}{e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y-2}^{0}{e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}[{\int }_{y-2}^{0}\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}\cdot x\,{|}_{y-2}^{0}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(2-y){e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={e}^{2y-{y}^{2}/2}\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & ={e}^{2(2)-{2}^{2}/2}-{e}^{2(0)-{0}^{2}/2} \\  & ={e}^{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$
